original_meaning_en: Body grime; dead skin that exfoliates
original_meaning_es: Mugre corporal; piel muerta que se exfolia
meaning_in_use_en: Accumulated dirt on skin especially in children
meaning_in_use_es: Mugre acumulada en la piel especialmente en niños
encoded_social_meaning_en: Working-class child; plays outside barefoot. Absent in upper-class contexts
encoded_social_meaning_es: Clase media-baja; niño que juega en calle a patapelá. Ausente en clase alta
typical_context_en: Before bath time: 'go get that piñén off'
typical_context_es: Antes del baño: 'a sacarse el piñén'
functional_translation_en: Body grime / dirt crust (no exact cultural equivalent)
cultural_notes_en: Term encodes a body that labors and plays outdoors without daily hygiene as privilege
cultural_notes_es: El término codifica un cuerpo que trabaja y juega afuera sin la higiene diaria como privilegio
claim_1_note: Attested via native speaker experience and family use. Lexicographic verification pending. Piñán rejected as variant — likely transcription artifact.

original_meaning_en: Mountain lion / lion of the mountain
meaning_in_use_en: The animal; also internationally known as a sports brand — almost nobody knows the word is Mapuche
meaning_in_use_es: El animal; también marca deportiva — casi nadie sabe que la palabra es mapuche
encoded_social_meaning_en: Global brand appropriation of indigenous vocabulary without attribution
encoded_social_meaning_es: Apropiación de vocabulario indígena por marca global sin atribución
typical_context_en: Referring to the animal or the sports brand
typical_context_es: Al referirse al animal o a la marca deportiva
cultural_notes_en: Paradigmatic case of invisible indigenous origin — the word travels the world with its Mapuche roots erased
cultural_notes_es: Caso paradigmático de origen indígena invisible — la palabra viaja el mundo con sus raíces mapuche borradas
claim_1_note: Widely cited as Mapuche origin. Zúñiga (2000) consulted — does not list puma as headword. Augusta and Catrileo pending.

meaning_in_use_en: Gossip; social drama; 'he said / she said' entanglement
meaning_in_use_es: Chisme; enredo social; 'que dijo / que no dijo'
encoded_social_meaning_en: Semantic degradation of a communal indigenous practice into a marker of social toxicity
encoded_social_meaning_es: Degradación semántica de una práctica indígena comunitaria hacia marcador de toxicidad social
typical_context_en: 'Se armó un cahuín' (drama broke out); 'no metas cahuín' (don't stir the pot)
functional_translation_en: Gossip / drama / stirring the pot (no exact equivalent)
cultural_notes_en: Semantic shift from sacred ritual to petty gossip encodes colonial displacement of Mapuche culture
cultural_notes_es: El desplazamiento semántico codifica el desplazamiento colonial de la cultura mapuche
claim_1_note: Chilenismo meaning well-attested. Original Mapudungún ritual meaning requires Augusta/Catrileo confirmation. The semantic shift itself is the core analytical datum.

original_meaning_en: ñuño = dandelion; -a = place suffix → 'place of dandelions'
original_meaning_es: ñuño = diente de león; -a = sufijo de lugar → 'lugar de los dientes de león'
meaning_in_use_en: Name of a commune in Santiago; no floral meaning survives in everyday use
meaning_in_use_es: Nombre de una comuna de Santiago; el significado floral no sobrevive en el uso cotidiano
encoded_social_meaning_en: Indigenous place names persist in urban maps while the culture that named them is displaced
encoded_social_meaning_es: Los topónimos indígenas persisten en mapas urbanos mientras la cultura que los nombró es desplazada
typical_context_es: Línea de metro, direcciones, referencias municipales
cultural_notes_en: Paradigmatic case of toponymic fossilization: Mapuche ecological geography as administrative label
cultural_notes_es: Caso paradigmático de fosilización toponímica: geografía mapuche como etiqueta administrativa
claim_1_note: Locative suffix pattern confirmed in Zúñiga (2000) via -ntu. Whether -a functions identically and botanical meaning of ñuño require Augusta (1916) confirmation.

original_meaning_en: Edible red seaweed (Pyropia columbina); pre-Hispanic coastal food source
original_meaning_es: Alga roja comestible (Pyropia columbina); alimento costero prehispánico
meaning_in_use_en: (1) Seaweed in soups/stews sold as 'pan de luche'; (2) hopscotch-like children's game
meaning_in_use_es: (1) Alga en guisos y cazuelas como 'pan de luche'; (2) juego infantil similar al rayuela
encoded_social_meaning_en: Double meaning connects coastal indigenous food culture with urban childhood play — both uses disappearing
encoded_social_meaning_es: El doble significado conecta cultura alimentaria indígena costera con juego infantil urbano — ambos desaparecen
typical_context_en: 'Vamos a jugar luche' / '¿Compraste luche en la feria?'
typical_context_es: 'Vamos a jugar luche' / '¿Compraste luche en la feria?'
cultural_notes_en: Rare case of indigenous-origin word covering both a food and a game; possible metaphorical extension
cultural_notes_es: Caso raro de palabra de origen indígena cubriendo alimento y juego; posible extensión metafórica
claim_1_note: Species verified: Pyropia columbina (confirmed SUBPESCA/FIPA). Common misattribution to Ulva lactuca corrected. Linguistic origin (Mapudungún vs Quechua) genuinely uncertain — marked disputed not unverified.

original_meaning_es: cocha = agua/lago + yuyo = hierba/maleza → 'hierba del agua'
meaning_in_use_en: Large brown seaweed (Durvillaea antarctica); staple of Chilean coastal and working-class cuisine
meaning_in_use_es: Alga parda grande (Durvillaea antarctica); alimento base de la cocina costera y popular chilena
encoded_social_meaning_en: Associated with working-class coastal diet; historically 'poor people's food' now revalorized as superfood
encoded_social_meaning_es: Asociado a dieta popular costera; históricamente 'comida de pobres' ahora revalorizado como superalimento
typical_context_en: 'Cazuela de cochayuyo'; sold dried in coastal markets from Coquimbo to Magallanes
typical_context_es: 'Cazuela de cochayuyo'; vendido seco en mercados costeros de Coquimbo a Magallanes
functional_translation_en: Bull kelp / cochayuyo (no exact English common name)
cultural_notes_en: Quechua origin reveals Andean trade networks that shaped Chilean coastal vocabulary — word traveled from inland lake cultures to Pacific coast
cultural_notes_es: El origen quechua revela redes de intercambio andinas — la palabra viajó desde culturas lacustres del interior hasta la costa del Pacífico
claim_1_note: Species verified: Durvillaea antarctica (confirmed SUBPESCA/FIPA). Note: two species (D. antarctica and D. incurvata) both called cochayuyo. Quechua etymology (cocha+yuyo) consistent with word-formation patterns; Ayacucho Quechua dictionary confirmation pending.
